headline: Advance whichever interval finishes first
statement: Given two sorted lists of pairwise-disjoint closed intervals, return every intersection between an interval from the first list and one from the second. Either list may be empty.
constraints: Within each list, intervals are sorted and pairwise disjoint
intuition: Compare one interval from each sorted list. Their shared part starts at the later start and ends at the earlier end. Save it if those boundaries meet. Then advance the interval that ends first, because it cannot overlap any later interval from the other list.
approach: Point i and j at the current intervals.
Compute low=max(starts) and high=min(ends); append [low,high] if low<=high.
Advance the pointer whose interval ends first; repeat while both remain.
correctness: At each step, the algorithm records the current pair’s exact intersection. If A ends before B, all later B intervals begin after B ends and hence after A ends; A has no untested future intersection. Discarding A is safe, and the symmetric argument applies to B. Thus every possible overlap is processed once.
bruteForce: Compare every interval in one list against every interval in the other, taking O(mn) time.

complexity.explanation: At least one pointer advances per iteration; result storage is O(m+n).

pitfalls: A single touching point is a valid closed intersection.
Advance by end time rather than start time.
